rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell lies in wait, watching over the disbelievers and those against whom punishment is decreed.
rows.anchor: يرصد أهل الكفر ومن حق عليه العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell nearly bursts with rage, and those sentenced to punishment cannot pass beyond it.
rows.anchor: تكاد تميز من الغيظ، فلا يجاوزها من حقت عليه كلمة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʾāb means the place to which the transgressors return.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (مآبا) إليها يرجعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source distinguishes lābith as one who stays from labith as one for whom staying has become characteristic.
rows.anchor: ويقال: هو لبث بمكان كذا أي صار اللبث شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of aḥqāb is ḥuqb, defined here as eighty years, each year twelve months and each month thirty days; each day equals a thousand worldly years.
rows.anchor: والأحقاب واحدها حقب، والحقب ثمانون سنة، كل سنة اثنا عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned remain ages without coolness or drink and remain in Hell forever, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: وهم خالدون في النار أبدا كما قال عز وجل: (خالدين فيها أبدا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed interpretation takes bard, “coolness,” to mean sleep.
rows.anchor: قيل نوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows bard to mean cool wind, shade, or sleep, none of which they taste in Hell.
rows.anchor: لا يذفقون فيها برد ريح ولا ظل ولا نوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīm is water at the utmost degree of heat.
rows.anchor: أي لا يذوقون فيها إلا حميما وهو في غاية الحرارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported explanation takes ghassāq as what flows from the skins of the damned.
rows.anchor: قيل ما يغسق من جلودهم، أي يسيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reported explanation takes ghassāq to mean intense cold.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الغساق الشديد البرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment corresponds to their deeds.
rows.anchor: أي جوزوا وفق أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the verse as disbelief in resurrection and accountability; the excerpt then says they “hope for the reward of reckoning.”
rows.anchor: لا يؤمنون بالبعث ولا بأنهم يحاسبون، ويرجون ثواب حساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light form of kidhāban is also read, while the doubled form is more common.
rows.anchor: وقد قرئت (كذابا) بالتخفيف. و (كذابا) بالتشديد أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For verbal nouns of faʿʿala, the pattern kidhāb is better than faʿʿāl.
rows.anchor: وهو في مصادر فعلت أجود من فعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's word qaḍāʾuhā illustrates the verbal noun qaḍāʾ for qaḍaytu.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: لقد طال ما ثبطتني عن صحابتي. . . وعن حوج قضاؤها من شفائيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses the light form kadhāb in “the person is helped by his lying,” supporting the light reading.
rows.anchor: ومثل كذابا - بالتخفيف قول الشاعر: فصدقتها وكذبتها. . . والمرء ينفعه كذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nakāl is an accusative verbal noun used as an emphatic cognate accusative: God took him by inflicting punishment.
rows.anchor: (نكال) منصوب مصدر مؤكد لأن معنى أخذه الله نكل به نكال الآخرة والأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drowned Pharaoh in this world and will punish him in the next.
rows.anchor: أي أغرقه في الدنيا ويعذبه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tafsīr explanation takes the two terms as punishment for Pharaoh's claims that he knew no god but himself and was the highest lord.
rows.anchor: نكال قوله: (ما علمت لكم من إله غيري). وقوله: (أنا ربكم الأعلى).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians attach banāhā to al-samāʾ as a relative clause: “or the one who built it.”
rows.anchor: قال بعض النحويين: (بناها) من صلة السماء، المعنى أم التي بناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say al-samāʾ does not take a relative clause here; the comparison is whether you or the sky is greater in creation.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: السماء ليس مما يوصل، ولكن المعنى أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء أشد خلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses aghṭasha as making the night dark.
rows.anchor: أي أظلم ليلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought forth the day's light by means of the sun.
rows.anchor: أظهر نورها بالشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is an accusative causal expression, meaning “because the blind man came.”
rows.anchor: (أن) في موضع نصب مفعول له، المعنى لأن جاءه الأعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, who came while the Prophet was calling Quraysh notables to Islam, hoping their conversion would draw others.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عبد الله ابن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet turned from Ibn Umm Maktūm to address the notables, so God instructed him not to neglect a Muslim by attending to someone else.
rows.anchor: فأمره الله ألا يتشاغل عن الإقبال على أحد من المسلمين بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading of tanfaʿahu makes it a result dependent on laʿalla.
rows.anchor: فمن نصب فعلى جواب (لعل)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading coordinates tanfaʿu with yuzakkā.
rows.anchor: ومن رفع فعلى العطف على (يزكى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressee attends to the person who considers himself self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: أي أنت تقبل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With light ṣād, taṣaddā derives from tataṣaddā, with the second tāʾ deleted where two tāʾs meet.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ (تصدى) - بتخفيف الصاد - فالأصل تتصدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading assimilates the tāʾ into ṣād; its underlying form and meaning are also tataṣaddā.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (تصدى) بإدغام التاء، فالمعنى أيضا تتصدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is: what responsibility is yours if the person you invite to Islam does not accept it?
rows.anchor: أي أي شيء عليك أن لا يسلم من تدعوه إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talahhā means to become occupied or distracted from something.
rows.anchor: معناه تتشاغل، يقال: لهيت عن الشيء ألهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is the admonition God gave the Prophet in this passage.
rows.anchor: يعنى به هذه الموعظة التي وعظ الله بها النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine pronoun is used because mawʿiẓa and waʿẓ are treated as one; the meaning addresses the bearers of the Qurʾān: whoever wills may remember it.
rows.anchor: ذكر لأن الموعظة والوعظ واحد، والمعنى راجع إلى حملة القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says the book is with Him in the Preserved Tablet, in honored, elevated, purified pages carried by angels.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر جل وعز أن الكتاب في اللوح المحفوظ عنده، فقال: (في صحف مكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safara are the scribes, meaning angels; safir is singular, following the pattern of kātib/kَataba and kāfir/kafara.
rows.anchor: والسفرة الكتبة، يعني به الملائكة، واحدهم سافر وسفرة مثل كاتب وكتبة، وكافر وكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms for the book and scribe express clarification: dawn brightens, a woman uncovers her face, and one who mediates discloses each party's feelings to reconcile them.
rows.anchor: لأن معناه أنه يبين الشيء ويوضحه، يقال أسفر الصبح إذا أضاء، وسفرت المرأة إذا كشفت النقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barara is the plural of bārr.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (كرام بررة (16) جمع بار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may express wonder at human disbelief, inviting the audience to marvel at it, like the wonder expressed in 2:175.
rows.anchor: أي اعجبوا أنتم من كفر الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a rebuke phrased as a question: “How ungrateful he is!”
rows.anchor: ويجوز على معنى التوبيخ ولفظه لفظ الاستفهام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is formally interrogative but functions as an assertion or reminder, then specifies what he was created from.
rows.anchor: على لفظ الاستفهام، ومعناه التقرير ثم بين فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faqaddarahu means God proportioned him properly, as another verse says He fashioned a person from dust, then a drop, and made him a man.
rows.anchor: المعنى فقدره على الاستواء كما قال عز وجل: (أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم سواك رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided the human along the way, whether grateful or ungrateful.
rows.anchor: أي هداه السبيل (إما شاكرا وإما كفورا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky splits on the Day of Resurrection with clouds.
rows.anchor: أي انشقت، تتشقق السماء يوم القيامة بالغمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars fall and scatter.
rows.anchor: أي تساقطت وتهافتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fresh water is made to flow into the salt water.
rows.anchor: فجر العذب إلى المالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The graves are overturned: their soil is turned over and their dead are resurrected.
rows.anchor: يعني بحثرت، أي قلب ترابها وبعث الموتى الذين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What a soul advanced is the commanded deed it performed; what it left behind is what it did not know.
rows.anchor: (ما قدمت) من عمل أمرت به وما (أخرت) منه فلم تعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is a precedent a person established, which was acted upon after them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وأخرت سنت من سنة - عمل بها بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gharra means to deceive and entice someone until they neglect what is due to God.
rows.anchor: أي ما خدعك وسول لك حتى أضعت ما وجب عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faʿadalaka means God formed you in the best proportion.
rows.anchor: أي خلقك في أحسن تقويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the light and doubled pronunciations of faʿadalaka are read.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ (فعدلك) بالتخفيف والتشديد جميعا

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mā is an emphatic extra particle, the sense is that God formed you in whichever shape He wished, tall or short, attractive or otherwise.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون (ما) صلة مؤكدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mā is conditional: in whatever shape He chose to form you, He formed you in it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما في معنى الشرط والجزاء، فيكون المعنى في أي صورة ما شاء أن يركبك فيها ركبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny resurrection, judgment, and recompense for their deeds.
rows.anchor: أي بل تكذبون بأنكم تبعثون وتدانون، أي تجازون بأعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels record against people what they do.
rows.anchor: فيكتبونه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-dīn is the Day of Recompense, the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يوم الجزاء وهو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated mention of the Day magnifies its importance.
rows.anchor: فكرر ذكر اليوم تعظيما لشأنه

words: يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِّنَفْسٍ شَيْـًٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads the verb with masculine agreement: yawm lā yamliku nafs.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (يوم) لا يملك نفس

words: يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِّنَفْسٍ شَيْـًٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nominative yawm, it can modify yawm al-dīn, or be raised with an implicit huwa.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ بالرفع فعلى أن اليوم صفة لقوله (يوم الدين)

words: يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِّنَفْسٍ شَيْـًٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm may also be nominative while built on fatḥ because it is annexed to the indeclinable clause lā tamliku; a poem similarly builds ghayr after its annexed clause.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع وهو مبني على الفتح

words: يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِّنَفْسٍ شَيْـًٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's ghayr an naṭaqat is built on fatḥ after being annexed to a clause.
rows.anchor: كما قال الشاعر: لم يمنع الشرب منها غير أن نطقت. . . حمامة في غصون ذات أوقال

words: يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِّنَفْسٍ شَيْـًٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm may instead be accusative, matching the meaning of the events just mentioned.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون نصبه على معنى هذه الأشياء المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raḥīq is an unmixed drink; Ḥassān's poetic word raḥīq describes the pure, flowing drink.
rows.anchor: قال حسان: يسقون من ورد البريص عليهم. . . بردى يصفق بالرحيق السلسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhtūm refers specifically to the drink's having run out; after the cup is emptied and drinking ends, it is sealed with musk's taste and scent.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (مختوم): في انقطاعه خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spring comes to the people of Paradise from above, wafting toward them from the chambers.
rows.anchor: تأتيهم من علو عينا تنسم عليهم من الغرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes ʿaynan an accusative object, as in the wording of 90:14.
rows.anchor: فعينا في هذا القول منصوبة مفعولة، كما قال: (أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة (14) يتيما)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ʿaynan is the object of yasqūn, meaning they drink from a spring.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون (عينا) منصوبة بقوله يسقون عينا، أي من عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis makes ʿaynan an accusative circumstantial, with tasnīm definite and ʿaynan indefinite.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون عينا منصوبا على الحال، ويكون (تسنيم) معرفة و (عينا) نكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people described were Quraysh disbelievers who mocked early Muslim followers of the Prophet, including ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, for accepting Islam.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء جماعة من كفار قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were pleased with themselves and amused themselves by talking about the believers.
rows.anchor: معجبيين بما هم فيه يتفكهون بذكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mockers were not appointed as guardians over the believers' deeds.
rows.anchor: أي ما أرسل هؤلاء القوم على أصحاب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يحفظون عليهم أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' laughter at the disbelievers takes place on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the disbelievers were repaid for mocking the believers in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي هل جوزوا بسخريتهم بالمؤمنين في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading assimilates the lām into the thāʾ in haththawwiba.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ هثوب، بإدغام اللام في الثاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky splits on the Day of Resurrection with clouds.
rows.anchor: تنشق يوم القيامة بالغمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to idhā is indicated by famulāqīhi: when Resurrection comes, a person meets his deed.
rows.anchor: المعنى إذا كان يوم القيامة لقي الإنسان عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhinat means “heard”; Arab usage says adhintu li-shayʾ when one hears something.
rows.anchor: أي سمعت، يقال: أذنت للشيء آذن إذا سمعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses adhinu to mean “they heard” in a line about those who hear praise or insult.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: صم إذا سمعوا خيرا ذكرت به. . . وإن ذكرت بسوء عندهم أذنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa ḥuqqat means it was right and proper for the sky to do so.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (وحقت) أي حق لها أن تفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is removed from its former shape and transformed.
rows.anchor: أزيلت عن هيئتها وبدلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth casts out the dead and its treasures.
rows.anchor: ألقت ما فيها من الموتى والكنوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsīr explains the phrase as doing work for one's Lord and meeting that work.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير إنك عامل لربك عملا فملاقيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another tafsīr explanation is striving toward one's Lord and meeting Him.
rows.anchor: وجاء أيضا: ساع إلى ربك سعيا فملاقيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, kadhḥ is exertion and persistent effort in work, whether worldly or otherworldly.
rows.anchor: في باب الدنيا وباب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamīm ibn Muqbil's phrase akdaḥ illustrates striving and toil in seeking a livelihood.
rows.anchor: قال تميم بن مقبل: وما الدهر إلا تارتان فمنهما. . . أموت وأخرى أبتغي العيش أكدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported explanation takes the object of “meeting” to be one's work.
rows.anchor: وقيل فملاق عملك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's report identifies the easy reckoning as presentation before God, and says whoever is closely questioned in the reckoning is punished.
rows.anchor: روينا عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن ذلك العرض على الله - عز وجل - وأنه من نوقش الحساب عذب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A second Prophetic report says that whoever is closely questioned in the reckoning perishes.
rows.anchor: وروينا أيضا أنه من نوقش الحساب هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cries “woe” or “destruction”; this is the cry of someone in ruin, specifically the one given his book behind his back.
rows.anchor: أي يقول: يا ويلاه، يا ثبوراه، وهذا يقوله من وقع في هلكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading of yuṣlā is glossed as meaning that his punishment is intensified.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (ويصلى سعيرا)، أي يكثر عذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person was happy with his family in worldly life.
rows.anchor: يعني في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This describes the believer, who returns happily to his family in the Gardens God prepared for His friends.
rows.anchor: فمن صفة المؤمن، وينقلب إلى أهله في الجنان التي أعدهن الله لأوليائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This describes the disbeliever, who thinks he will not return, meaning he will not be resurrected.
rows.anchor: هذه صفة الكافر ظن أن لن يحور بأن لن يبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, yaḥūr means to return to God.
rows.anchor: ومعنى يحور - في اللغة - أن يرجع إلى الله عز وجل

words: بَلَىٰٓ إِنَّ رَبَّهُۥ كَانَ بِهِۦ بَصِيرًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew the person before creating him and knows that his return is to Him.
rows.anchor: قبل أن يخلقه، عالما بأن مرجعه إليه - عز وجل -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses dāfiq as coming from above.
rows.anchor: معناه من فوق

rows.speaker: سيبويه وأصحابه
rows.claim: Sibawayh and his associates derive dāfiq by relation to effusion: it means water possessing an effusion.
rows.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه وأصحابه أن معناه النسب إلى الاندفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One tafsīr report identifies the tarāʾib as four ribs on each side of the chest.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنها أربعة أضلاع من يمنة الصدر وأربع أضلاع من يسرة الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second tafsīr report identifies the tarāʾib as the hands, feet, and eyes.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن الترائب اليدان والرجلان والعينان

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: The language authorities unanimously locate the tarāʾib at the necklace area of the chest.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة أجمعون: الترائب موضع القلادة من الصدر

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's word tarāʾibahā describes a woman's polished chest and supports the chest-area sense.
rows.anchor: وأنشدوا لامرئ القيس: مهفهفة بيضاء غير مفاضة. . . ترائبها مصقولة كالسجنجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One tafsīr explanation takes the return as the water's return to the urethra.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير: على رجع الماء إلى الإحليل لقادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the return as the water's return to the loins.
rows.anchor: وجاء أيضا على رجعه إلى الصلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He favors the interpretation that God can resurrect the human, supported by the mention of the day secrets are tested.
rows.anchor: وجاء أيضا على رجعه على بعث الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is described as having recurring rain, which comes back repeatedly.
rows.anchor: (ذات الرجع) ذات المطر لأنه يجيء ويرجع ويتكرر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses rajʿ as water and cites al-Munkhal al-Hudhalī's word al-rajʿ to compare a sword's whiteness to water.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الرجع: الماء، وأنشد بيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth splits open with vegetation.
rows.anchor: أي تصدع بالنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer refers to the Qurʾān, which distinguishes truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم يعنى به القرآن، يفصل بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is not play or frivolity.
rows.anchor: ما هو باللعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers plot against the Prophet, pretending to show something other than what they intend.
rows.anchor: يعني به الكفار، أنهم يحاتلون النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's counter-scheme is to draw them gradually toward punishment without their awareness.
rows.anchor: كيد الله لهم استدراجهم من حيث لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruwaydan means “a little”; God is to give them a brief respite.
rows.anchor: أي أمهلهم قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn means recompense; the proverb “as you act, you are repaid” expresses repayment according to one's deeds.
rows.anchor: الدين في اللغة الجزاء، يقال: كما تدين تدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn can also mean custom; Arabs say mā zāla dhālika dīnī, “that has always been my custom.”
rows.anchor: تقول العرب ما زال ذلك ديني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses dīn to mean one's custom in the phrase “Is that ever his custom and mine?”
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: تقول إذا درات لها وضيني. . . أهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIbāda means obedience together with humility; the phrase means that we obey God with submission.
rows.anchor: معنى العبادة في اللغة الطاعة مع الخضوع، يقال هذا طريق معبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A road is called maʿbad when much foot traffic has subdued it, and a camel is maʿbad when coated with tar.
rows.anchor: وبعير معبد، إذا كان مطليا بالقطران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iyyāka is the accusative object, while its kāf is genitive through annexation to iyyā; iyyā is a noun used for accusative pronouns and may take any such pronoun.
rows.anchor: وموضع (إياك) نصب بوقوع الفعل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding iyyā to an overt noun, as in iyyā Zayd, is inelegant because it is reserved for pronouns.
rows.anchor: كان قبيحا لأنه خص به المضمر

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl transmits an Arab expression warning a man over sixty to beware of young women, with iyyā used before a noun.
rows.anchor: رواه الخليل: (إذا بلغ الرجل الستين فإياه وإيا الشواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that iyyāka is one indivisible noun: nouns do not take annexation this way, while Arabic treats the hāʾ of iyyāhu like that in ʿaṣāhu.
rows.anchor: ومن قال إن إياك بكماله الاسم، قيل له:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nastaʿīnu originally was nastaʿūnu, from maʿūna and ʿawn; wāw became yāʾ under the weight of kasra, the kasra moved to ʿayn, and the resulting sound changes follow examples like aʿāna/yaʿīnu.
rows.anchor: الأصل في نستعين: نستعون لأنه إنما معناه من المعونة والعون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the clear way; an unnamed poet uses ṣirāṭ for a clear road.
rows.anchor: معناه المنهاج الواضح قال الشاعر: أمير المؤمنين على صراط. . . إذا اعوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Guide us” means “keep us firm in guidance,” like asking a person already standing to remain so until one returns.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (اهدنا وهم مهتدون: ثبتنا على الهدى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an adjective for al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm.
rows.anchor: صفة لقوله عز وجل: (الصراط المستقيم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hāʾ in ʿalayhim may carry ḍamma or kasra, the two forms used by most readers; a form with an added wāw is also possible.
rows.anchor: ولك في عليهم ضم الهاء وكسرها (تقول: الذين أنعمت عليهم وعليهم)

rows.speaker: سِيبَوَيْهِ
rows.claim: Sībawayh says the wāw added after masculine hāʾ parallels the added alif in feminine hāʾ forms.
rows.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أن الواو زيدت على الهاء في المذكر كما زيدت الألف في المؤنث

rows.speaker: أصحاب سيبويه والخليل
rows.claim: Sībawayh's and al-Khalīl's associates explain the added wāw as clarifying the faint hāʾ; it disappears in pause and is not retained as an original letter.
rows.anchor: والقول في هذه الواو عند أصحاب سيبويه والخليل أنها إنما زيدت لخفاء الهاء وذلك أن الهاء تخرج من أقصى الحلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a preceding kasra the wāw may change to yāʾ; the Hijazi readings of 28:81 include both hī and hū forms.
rows.anchor: فإذا قلت: مررت -، بهو - يا فتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs are reported to use a kasra with the second-person kāf in ʿalaykum and bikum, but he rejects this as an anomalous dialect; the correct poetic wording is faḍl aḥlāmikum.
rows.anchor: روي عن بعض العرب: (عليكم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh quotes the poem with the anomalous form, though its sound transmission is faḍl aḥlāmikum.
rows.anchor: وهذه لغة شاذة، والرواية الصحيحة: فضل أحلامكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural hāʾ forms originally had a wāw, but speakers omit it because mīm suffices and the wāw is heavy; Arabic names do not end in wāw preceded by a vowel.
rows.anchor: ولكن الميم استغنى بها عن الواو، والواو تثقل على ألسنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with the wāw in ʿalayhumū is rare; he says the widespread form without it should be read.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي أن يقرأ إلا بالكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With genitive ghayr, one analysis makes it a substitute for alladhīna, yielding “the path of those other than the angered.”
rows.anchor: فيخفض (غير) على وجهين، على البدل من الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, genitive ghayr qualifies alladhīna; although ghayr usually describes an indefinite noun, alladhīna here denotes a category rather than particular people.
rows.anchor: من صفة الذين، وإن كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative ghayr can be an exception, equivalent to “except the angered”; exception ghayr is accusative when what follows illā is accusative.
rows.anchor: ويجوز نصب (غير) على ضربين: على الحال وعلى الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative ghayr can instead be a circumstantial, meaning the path of those blessed, not angered.
rows.anchor: فأما الحال فكأنك قلت فيها: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم لا مغضوبا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍāllīn is coordinated with al-maghḍūb ʿalayhim; lā is allowed because ghayr already carries negation, as in ghayr ḍārib meaning “not striking.”
rows.anchor: فإنما عطف بالضالين على المغضوب عليهم، وإنما جاز أن يقع (لا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One cannot say mithla ḍārib in the parallel construction, because Zayd depends on ḍārib and cannot precede it.
rows.anchor: ولا يجيزون أنت زيدا مثل ضارب، لأن زيدا من صلة ضارب فلا يتقدم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After praise and supplication, Arabs use both Amīn and Āmīn; two poems attest the forms.
rows.anchor: قول القائلين بعد الفراغ من الحمد، ومن الدعاء " آمين " فيه لغتان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses Amīn in a prayer that God increase the distance between the speaker and Fataḥl.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: تباعد عني فطحل إذ دعوته. . . أمين فزاد الله ما بيننا بعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another unnamed poet uses Āmīnā in a prayer for God's mercy on one who says it.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر أيضا: يا رب لا تسلبني حبها أبدا. . . ويرحم الله عبدا قال آمينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amīn and Āmīn mean “O God, answer”; they stand in place of a verbal noun for response, like ṣah standing for silence.
rows.anchor: ومعناه: اللهم استجب، وهما موضوعان في موضع اسم الاستجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both are normally paused sounds rather than verb-derived forms; nūn is opened to resolve adjacent quiescent letters, since kasra is heavy after yāʾ, as in ayna and kayfa.
rows.anchor: وحقهما من الإعراب الوقف لأنهما بمنزلة الأصوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author presents the work as a concise book on Qurʾānic parsing and meanings and asks God for success in all matters.
rows.anchor: هذا كتاب مختصر في إعراب القرآن ومعانيه، ونسأل الله التوفيق في كل الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ supplies the sense of beginning: “I began in the name of God”; the verb “I began” is omitted because the situation makes it clear.
rows.anchor: الجالب للباء معنى الابتداء، كأنك قلت: بدأت باسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first alif in ism is hamzat waṣl, used to pronounce an initial consonant cluster; it disappears phonetically, as shown by the diminutive and forms ism and sim.
rows.anchor: وسقطت الألف من باسم الله في اللفظ وكان الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diminutive samī and Arab forms ism and sim, together with a rajaz line using simah, support the hamzat-waṣl analysis.
rows.anchor: قال الراجز: باسم الذي في كل سورة سمه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ism derives from sumū, “elevation”; its original form is sumw, and its plural asmāʾ follows patterns such as qanū/aqnāʾ and ḥanū/aḥnāʾ.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قولنا اسم: إنه مشتق من السمو، والسمو الرفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A name draws attention to God's name through its meaning, since the meaning lies beneath the name.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل الاسم تنويها باسم الله على المعنى؛ لأن المعنى تحت الإسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects derivation from wasama, “to mark”: it would require a root-initial wāw to disappear after hamzat waṣl, unlike the patterns of ʿidda and zina.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: إن اسما مأخوذ من " وسمت " فهو غلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ism came from wasama, its diminutive should be wasīm, like waʿīda and waṣīla from words whose root-initial wāw is dropped; this is not the case.
rows.anchor: فلو كان " اسم " وسمة لكان تصغيره إذا حذفت منه ألف الوصل " وسيم "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing omits the alif in bism Allāh but retains it in bi-smi rabbika; omission in the basmala reflects its spoken elision and frequent use.
rows.anchor: وسقطت الألف في الكتاب من " بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم "

rows.speaker: سِيبَوَيْهِ
rows.claim: Sībawayh says bāʾ means attachment: writing with a pen means the writing is attached to the pen.
rows.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أن معنى الباء الإلصاق، تقول كتبت بالقلم والمعنى أن الكتابة ملصقة بالقلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi is always kasra because it governs genitive; its vowel distinguishes the particle bi-Zayd from the noun kā-Zayd, which also governs genitive.
rows.anchor: وهي مكسورة أبدا لأنه - لا معنى لها إلا الخفض
